board_authority: Board of Secondary Education, Andhra Pradesh (BSEAP)
ownership: Government (also followed by many private/aided schools)
passing_criteria: Pass mark ~35% per subject; grading is now largely Grade-Point based under BSEAP
next_step: Choose one: Intermediate (MPC/BiPC/CEC/MEC/HEC) via bieap.apcfss.in, AP POLYCET for a diploma, ITI for a trade certificate, or NIOS if unable to continue formal school
approx_fee: Free / nominal in government schools; govt-aided schools may charge small fees

ownership: Private (a smaller number are Central Govt schools like KVs/JNVs)
medium_of_instruction: English (most common); some Hindi/Telugu medium sections
next_step: Same downstream choices as SSC students: Intermediate/Junior College (can continue CBSE Class 11-12 or move to AP Intermediate board), POLYCET diploma, or ITI
approx_fee: Varies widely by school (typically Rs 20,000 - Rs 2,00,000+/year) - unverified, needs school-by-school follow-up

board_authority: Council for the Indian School Certificate Examinations (CISCE)
classes_covered: Classes 1-10 (10 is the board-exam year, called ICSE)
passing_criteria: Minimum ~33-35 marks out of 100 per subject to pass (theory + internal/practical)
next_step: Same downstream options as CBSE/SSC students; ICSE is explicitly recognised as an equivalent qualifying board for AP Intermediate admission
approx_fee: Typically among the higher-fee private school options - exact figures vary per school, unverified
source: collegedekho.com ICSE passing marks guide; brinto.in AP Intermediate admission guide

board_authority: Navodaya Vidyalaya Samiti (NVS), Ministry of Education, Govt of India - CBSE affiliated
ownership: Government (Central Govt, fully residential and free)
classes_covered: Classes 6-12 (main entry at Class 6; limited lateral entry at Class 9)
medium_of_instruction: Three-language formula: English, Hindi, and Telugu, shifting toward English/Hindi in later classes
exam_window: Application ~Aug-Oct of preceding year; Phase-1 exam typically mid-January
passing_criteria: Selection-test merit rank; 75% seats reserved for rural-area students, 33% for girls, plus SC/ST/EWS/PwD reservations
next_step: Continues within the same JNV to Class 11-12, then the same downstream entrance exams as other CBSE students (AP EAPCET, NEET, etc.)
approx_fee: Free (tuition, boarding, food, uniforms, books all provided at no cost)
source: education.sakshi.com JNVST 2026 guide; en.wikipedia.org Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalaya

board_authority: Sainik Schools Society, Ministry of Defence, Govt of India - CBSE affiliated
ownership: Government (Central Govt, residential; boys and girls)
medium_of_instruction: English (CBSE English-medium), with NCC/military-style training alongside academics
key_exam: AISSEE (All India Sainik Schools Entrance Examination)
passing_criteria: Age criteria per entry class; merit in AISSEE + medical fitness; girls admitted against ~10% reserved quota
next_step: Continues within Sainik School to Class 11-12 (Science stream common), preparing directly for the NDA/NA entrance exam after Class 12
approx_fee: Approx. Rs 1.92 lakh/year at Sainik School Korukonda (AP), fees vary by category (SC/ST/OBC concessions apply)
source: selectyouruniversity.com AISSEE 2026 exam details; ezyschooling.com Sainik School Korukonda profile

school_type: Rashtriya Military School (RMS) - none located in AP
board_authority: Rashtriya Military Schools Society, Ministry of Defence, Govt of India - CBSE affiliated
exam_window: Cycle broadly similar to other Central Govt defence-school CETs - exact 2026 AP-relevant dates not independently verified
passing_criteria: Age criteria per entry class; boys only; open to defence-personnel and civilian applicants
next_step: No RMS is physically located in Andhra Pradesh (5 RMS at Ajmer, Bangalore, Belgaum, Chail, Dholpur); leads to Class 11-12 Science and NDA/NA preparation, same as Sainik Schools
approx_fee: Central Govt subsidised fees (lower than most CBSE private schools) - exact current figure not verified
source: sainikcoaching.web.app Rashtriya Military Schools locations & admission guide

school_type: AP Gurukulam Residential Schools (APSWREIS / APTWREIS / APMJPBCWREIS / APREIS)
board_authority: Respective AP Welfare Societies - Social/Tribal/BC Welfare / General Residential Educational Institutions Societies, Govt of Andhra Pradesh
ownership: Government (State Govt, residential, largely free for eligible community students)
classes_covered: Classes 5-12 (main entry at Class 5 via joint APGPCET; lateral entry at Classes 6-9 via society-specific CETs)
key_exam: APGPCET (joint 5th-class entrance test) or society-specific tests: APSWRS CET (SC), APTWRS CET (ST), APBCWRS CET (BC), APRS CET (general/open)
exam_window: Notifications and entrance tests typically run Feb-Apr each academic year
passing_criteria: Community-specific eligibility (SC/ST/BC/general); admission by merit rank in the relevant CET
next_step: Continues within the same society to Class 11-12 via RJC CET, then optionally RDC CET for degree-level admission inside the Gurukulam system, or external entrance exams after Class 12
approx_fee: Free or heavily subsidised for eligible community students

board_authority: Ministry of Tribal Affairs, Govt of India, implemented in AP via APTWREIS (Gurukulam) - CBSE affiliated
ownership: Government (Central Govt scheme, residential, ST students only)
classes_covered: Classes 6-12 (main entry at Class 6; Class 7/8 entry only against backlog vacancies)
passing_criteria: Open only to Scheduled Tribe (ST) students, priority to PVTG students in remote areas; merit rank in the CET
next_step: Continues to Class 12 within the EMRS (CBSE board), then the same downstream entrance-exam pathways as other CBSE students
approx_fee: Free (fully funded Central Govt scheme for ST students)

school_type: NIOS (National Institute of Open Schooling) - Secondary Course
board_authority: National Institute of Open Schooling (NIOS), autonomous body under Ministry of Education, Govt of India
ownership: Government (open/distance schooling - alternative to formal day school)
classes_covered: Equivalent to Class 10 (self-paced); AP & Telangana served by NIOS Regional Centre, Hyderabad
medium_of_instruction: Learner's choice among 17+ languages including Telugu, English, Hindi, Urdu; 24 subjects offered at Secondary level
key_exam: NIOS Secondary Public Examination, or the On-Demand Examination System (ODES) after the first attempt
exam_window: Two public exams per year (April-May and October-November); ODES available roughly monthly thereafter
passing_criteria: Minimum age 14; NIOS accepts self-declaration of having 'studied enough' rather than mandating a Class 8 pass certificate
next_step: NIOS Secondary certificate is recognised at par with SSC/CBSE/ICSE Class 10 for all further admissions, including AP Intermediate, POLYCET, and ITI
approx_fee: Nominal registration + exam fees (concessions for girls, SC/ST, disabled, and BPL learners)
source: rcdelhi.nios.ac.in NIOS FAQs; nios.ac.in official site
